newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam central bank says no rate change for now.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam central bank says no rate change for now.

text.p: The central State Bank of Vietnam said on Monday it had no plans to accelerate depreciation of Vietnam's currency, the dong, but left open the possibility that a move could still happen in the near future.
Vu Phuong Lien, the bank's deputy director of foreign exchange, told Reuters the dollar-dong exchange rate had already been adjusted this year.

"We do not have any new policy on foreign exchange, yet," she said, when asked if the bank might seek to quicken the pace of depreciation in line with recent currency movements elsewhere in the region.

Vietnam's central bank widened the margins of the interbank trading band in March from one percent to five percent on either side of a pivot rate, causing an almost instant fall of around four percent in the value of the dong against the dollar.
Since then it has followed a policy of gradual depreciation, by generally edging the pivot rate higher.

The dong was trading close to the band's upper limit on Monday at 11,683 to the dollar, but foreign bankers said dollars remained difficult to come by. A minor downwards adjustment, which saw the rate moved on Monday from 11,129 to 11,127, was dismissed as meaningless.

Treasury experts said they were expecting some move by the central bank to depreciate the currency in the near future in order to maintain export competitiveness, but a further widening of the interbank trading band was seen as an unlikely option.
"My personal view is that they may seek to speed up this weekly depreciation, by increasing movements of the pivot rate by around 10 or 12 dong per week from two or three," said one Western banker.
"Or, they will make a one-off adjustment of the rate and effectively link that to the developments in Thailand, Manila, etc," he added.
The dong was quoted at around 11,710 to the dollar on unofficial markets on Monday.
